title: Pronomen und sein — du oder Sie?
summary: The subject pronouns, the verb sein (to be), and your first du-vs-Sie decision

blocks.title: The people words
blocks.body: These are the subject pronouns — who's doing the verb. Two things to notice: German has **three** ways to say "you" (*du* casual-singular, *ihr* casual-plural, *Sie* formal), and there are **three** words that sound like *sie* — but context and the verb always sort them out.

blocks.title: sein — to be (learn it whole)
blocks.body: *sein* is irregular and everywhere, so memorize it as a block. **ich bin, du bist, er/sie/es ist, wir sind, ihr seid, sie/Sie sind.** Watch the *ihr* form: it's *seid* with a **d**, not a t.

blocks.title: sein in the wild — tap to hear
du vs Sie — the choice you make constantly

pairs.note: du: friends, family, kids, most people your age. Sie: strangers, officials, older people, at work. Unsure with an adult you don't know? Start with Sie — we master the switch in week 11.

blocks.explain: *ihr seid* — the ihr-form is *seid*, spelled with a d. Don't confuse it with *seit* (since).

blocks.prompt: Fill in the sein form: 'Wir ___ aus Kanada.' (we are from Canada)
blocks.explain: *wir sind* — and note *sie/Sie sind* uses the same form.

blocks.title: Build a 'to be' sentence
blocks.prompt: Pick a subject, match its sein form, and finish it off.

blocks.scene: At a friend's Feierabend get-together, Jonas introduces himself. Everyone here says du.

lines.speaker: Jonas
lines.nl: Hallo! Ich bin Jonas. Und du?
lines.spotlight: Casual *und du?* — he's on du from the first breath.

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Hallo Jonas. Ich bin neu hier. Ich bin aus Toronto.
lines.en: Hi Jonas. I'm new here. I'm from Toronto.

lines.speaker: Jonas
lines.nl: Cool! Bist du auch müde? Es ist schon spät.
lines.en: Cool! Are you tired too? It's late already.

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Ein bisschen. Aber es ist gemütlich hier.
lines.en: A little. But it's cozy here.

questions.q: Does Jonas address you formally or casually?
Where are you from in the dialogue?

blocks.prompt: Introduce yourself with sein: your name, where you're from, and one word for how you are today (müde? froh? nervös?).
